title: Outbound NAT election and DNS shadowing — upgrade proposal
content:
Summary:

This doc proposes a safe, reversible upgrade to the outbound networking design used by Private deployments (VPC + on-prem installations) to address two recurring issues: stale NAT mappings during burst failover, and DNS inconsistency across multi-zone/private-forwarder topologies (what we call "DNS shadowing"). The goal is to provide deterministic outbound IP behavior for customers, improve failover time, and standardize Terraform module interfaces for the rollout.

Design goals (non-exhaustive):
- Deterministic outbound IP per workload class (control vs. data) with optional sticky-source behavior.
- Fast NAT controller election with health-check based failover (avoid 60s+ delays).
- Centralized private-DNS shadowing: local forwarders per VPC/zone that are authoritative for split zones, with consistent TTL and fallback rules.
- Minimal customer infra changes (most logic lives in modules and a light controlplane agent).
- Rollout must be reversible with zero-config rollback path.

High-level architecture:
- NAT controller: lightweight controller (k8s DaemonSet) that configures iptables/ipvs rules on selected egress nodes. Election is done with a lease + external TCP healthchecks to upstream NAT hardware where applicable.
- Egress classes: workloads are labeled by policy: egress=control or egress=data. Terraform module provides NodeSelector / taints for egress nodes.
- Sticky NAT: optional 5-minute source-IP affinity implemented via conntrack tuning + controller-managed SNAT pools.
- DNS shadowing: each VPC has a dns-forwarder (dnsmasq/PowerDNS) that: 1) answers split-horizon zones from local records, 2) forwards customer-private zones to customer-provided forwarders and 3) falls back to Redwood forwarders if unreachable.

Why this differs from existing notes: most prior drafts focused purely on TF modules or on egress NAT scale; this proposal combines an explicit controller election algorithm, operational healthchecks, and a DNS shadowing policy that reduces cross-zone inconsistency.

Terraform module notes (interface and semantics):
- Module: redwood_private_egress (root module for egress setup)
  - inputs (key ones):
    - name_prefix (string)
    - egress_node_count (number)
    - snat_pool_cidrs (list of strings)  # customer-provided egress IP pools
    - enable_sticky_snat (bool)
    - sticky_timeout_seconds (number)
    - dns_forwarder_image (string)
    - dns_split_zones (list of strings)
    - controller_image (string)
    - healthcheck_port (number)
  - outputs:
    - controller_endpoint (string)
    - dns_forwarder_endpoints (list of strings)

Implementation notes for TF authors: keep resource names predictable for audit streams. Prefer names like ${var.name_prefix}-egress-controller-${count.index}. Use lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true } on controller DaemonSet node selectors so elections don't leave a gap.

Controller election algorithm (summary):
- Use k8s Lease API with 15s renewal interval and 45s deadline.
- Controller performs an additional application-level probing: open TCP to upstream NAT/node-route-appliance on configured port (healthcheck_port) every 5s; failover triggers fast path if three consecutive probes fail.
- When lease holder changes, the controller performs a two-phase switch: 1) program new SNAT mappings on candidate nodes, 2) signal old node to gracefully drain (conntrack timeouts allowed to expire but actively send RSTs for new connections if configured).

DNS shadowing rules (operator-facing):
- Local forwarders are authoritative only for explicitly-configured split zones. Example: customer.example.internal is owned locally; entries are managed via terraform var dns_zone_records or API.
- Resolution order inside a VPC: 1) local cache/hosts, 2) local forwarder authoritative zones, 3) forward to customer zone forwarders (if configured), 4) fallback to redwood-global-forwarder.
- TTLs: enforce minimum TTL=30s for critical internal entries to speed updates during failover.
- Observability: counts of NXDOMAIN by zone + latency histograms; expose in Console under per-deployment DNS tab.

Firewall and network policy conventions:
- Firewall rule names: ${prefix}-fw-egress-<tier>-<proto>-<port>-<region> (e.g., rwd-fw-egress-data-tcp-443-uswest2).
- Default egress deny at cluster CNI level; allowlist enforced by NetworkPolicy CRs scoped by namespace; TF module will generate NetworkPolicies on install unless opt-out.
- Control plane egress (KMS, controlplane API) is allowed via dedicated SNAT pool (smaller CIDR), separate audit logs.

NAT scaling and session affinity details:
- SNAT_pool sizing guidance: estimate = avg_concurrent_connections_per_pod * number_of_pods / 0.6 (to keep headroom).
- Affinity: sticky allocations use hashed allocation on 5-tuple with per-workload labels to prefer same SNAT IP. Implement by reserving /29 blocks per node group and programming SNAT rules to match source CIDR blocks.

Upgrade plan (safe path):
1) Canary setup in a single low-traffic deployment zone (zone-alpha) — deploy controller + dns-forwarder via module with enable_sticky_snat=false.
2) Validate connectivity: run p95/p99 egress latency tests and dns resolution checks (commands below).
3) Enable sticky_snat in canary, validate session stickiness for long-lived flows (websockets, health streams).
4) Roll to 10% of nodes (label-driven), monitor for: increased 5xx, dnscache misses, conntrack table sizes.
5) Full rollout with rolling updates and controller lease overlap window configured to 60s to minimize race.

Verification checklist (commands and probes):
- DNS checks: dig +trace customer.internal @<local-forwarder>
- Outbound IP check: curl --silent https://ifconfig.co -H 'Host: redwood-check'
- Session continuity: open websockets or tcpdump on upstream to ensure same SNAT IP for duration > sticky_timeout_seconds
- Conntrack: watch conntrack -L | wc -l (on node) and ensure count stays below 75% of conntrack-max after rollout.
- Latency: run artillery or wrk to simulate ephemeral connections; watch p95 tokenization/latency graphs in Console.

Suggested commands (examples):
- dig @10.10.1.2 customer.internal A +nocmd +noall +answer
- kubectl -n rwd-egress exec -it dns-forwarder-0 -- cat /etc/dnsmasq.conf
- curl -s https://ifconfig.co/json | jq .ip
- iperf3 -c <upstream-egress> -t 60 -P 10

Rollback plan (fast revert):
- TF destroy or set module enable flags to false with create_before_destroy semantics to bring back previous controller pods.
- Repoint dnsmasq forwarding to previous upstream list via var change and force rolling restart of dns-forwarder daemonset.
- Remove sticky_snat by setting sticky_timeout_seconds=0 and let conntrack age naturally.

Risk assessment and mitigations: 
- Risk: conntrack table exhaustion during sudden traffic surges. Mitigation: preflight sizing checks; set kernel conntrack_max via daemonset during upgrade; provide auto-shed option to drop new connections when above 85% capacity.
- Risk: inconsistent DNS during partial rollout. Mitigation: increase TTLs temporarily and use health checks that validate both DNS answer and end-to-end connectivity before marking node healthy.
- Risk: mis-sized SNAT pool leads to large egress IP usage. Mitigation: telemetry-driven recommendations in Redwood Console plus guard-rail that warns on >80% utilization.

Operational runbook (short):
- On alert 'egress-conntrack-usage-high': scale controller to 2x, enable connection-shed, and open immediate paging to on-call.
- On 'dns-forwarder-5xx' alert: rotate forwarder to fallback chain, restart dns-forwarder pods with previous working config, and roll back terraform change if >3% of queries error.

Open questions (to resolve before final):
- Do we require HSM-backed IP allocation pool management for regulated customers? (security/infra tradeoff)
- Should sticky_snat be opt-in per-namespace or per-workload? Per-namespace recommended for tenancy clarity.
- How to surface per-workload SNAT allocation in Console without exposing raw IP lists? Consider aggregated counters + hash bucket views.

Appendix — example TF usage (text snippet):
module "rwd_egress" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//private-egress"
  name_prefix = "customer-a-prod"
  egress_node_count = 3
  snat_pool_cidrs = ["198.51.100.0/29","198.51.100.8/29"]
  enable_sticky_snat = true
  sticky_timeout_seconds = 300
  dns_forwarder_image = "rwd/dns-forwarder:v1.2.0"
  dns_split_zones = ["customer.internal"]
}

Notes for the release owner:
- Release owner: Lina Park; backup: Miguel Gomez.
- Pre-announce to customers with private deployments: 2 weeks notice if sticky_snat will change egress IPs used for control-plane integrations.
- Create a CoPilot runbook (one-pager) for SREs that includes quick rollback commands and dashboard links.

If you are reviewing: please comment on the sticky_snat default (true vs false), and whether per-namespace opt-in is required for your use-cases.
